# firezone_client (Data Source)

Looks up an enrolled Client device by id, name, or firezone_id. Exactly one of the three must be set. Clients enroll themselves on first connect, so there is no firezone_client resource - this is lookup only.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Clients enroll themselves when a device first connects, so Terraform
# can reference one but never create it - hence a data source with no
# matching resource.

data "firezone_client" "by_id" {
  id = "42a7f82f-831a-4a9d-8f17-c66c2bb6e205"
}

# Prefer firezone_id over name for anything long-lived: names are not
# unique and change when a user renames their device, while the Firezone
# ID is stable. Both are filtered server-side, so either costs one
# request.
data "firezone_client" "by_firezone_id" {
  firezone_id = "fz-abc123"
}

# Looking up by name fails if more than one Client shares it.
data "firezone_client" "by_name" {
  name = "jane-laptop"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `firezone_id` (String) The device's stable Firezone ID. Set exactly one of id, name, or firezone_id. Unlike name, this survives a rename, which makes it the better key for a long-lived config.
- `id` (String) Client ID. Set exactly one of id, name, or firezone_id.
- `name` (String) Client name, as shown in the dashboard. Set exactly one of id, name, or firezone_id. Client names are not unique - the lookup fails if more than one matches.

### Read-Only

- `actor_id` (String) ID of the Actor this Client belongs to.
- `ipv4` (String) The Client's Firezone IPv4 address.
- `ipv6` (String) The Client's Firezone IPv6 address.
- `online` (Boolean) Whether the Client is currently connected. This is live state - expect it to differ between plan and apply, and don't build configuration decisions on it.
- `verified` (Boolean) Whether an admin has verified this device. Policies can require it via the client_verified condition property.
